clue.text: Feeling sick in the head?

parts.note: read literally it is a bout of nausea or headache; cryptically it is a sickness that exists only in the mind, the belief that one is ill

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person feels queasy or has a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the twist: the sickness is not felt in the head but imagined there.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition is anxious, unfounded conviction of illness, literally a feeling of sickness that lives only in the mind.

clue.text: Journalist supports one in army having been promoted?

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits beneath it, so the editor comes last
in tells us the word for one sits within the word for army

parts.note: a host is a large army or multitude
one is the Roman numeral I
ED is the usual crossword abbreviation for editor, a senior journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter backs a soldier who has just been given a higher rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a playful definition: being hoisted is literally being raised up, a jokey take on promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise up, so someone lifted to a higher position has in a sense been raised, a jocular synonym.

clue.text: Regularly appraised, admitting look's plain

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other
regularly picks every other letter of the word appraised, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: An assessor judges that someone's appearance is unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective describing the look, but it is a noun, open grassland. The 's is just 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide open expanse of flat grassland, a plain in the North American interior.

clue.text: Queen enters palace to put out Queen

indicators.note: put out suggests something disturbed or knocked out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R, for Regina, is the standard abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A monarch arrives at her palace, displeased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen enters' puts R among the letters of PALACE TO, and 'put out' rearranges the whole lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The last ruling pharaoh of Ptolemaic Egypt was a famous queen, lover of Mark Antony.

clue.text: Theatre occupied vacant time

indicators.note: vacant means emptied of its contents, so only the outside letters of occupied remain

parts.note: an eon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: A playhouse filled a free slot in its schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupied' and 'vacant' are opposites, which makes the surface paradoxical; emptying occupied leaves OD.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a name used for cinemas and, from the ancient Greek, a building for musical performances, so a kind of theatre.

clue.text: Small present, revolting pants

indicators.note: revolting here means turning over, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a reward is something given, a present

explanation.surface: A little gift turns out to be awful underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' turns S REWARD round; 'pants' looks like slang for rubbish but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawers is an old-fashioned word for underpants, and in Britain pants means underwear rather than trousers.

clue.text: Endlessly abuse a Republican getting cut off

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter of the word for abuse is lost

parts.note: to insult is to abuse verbally

explanation.surface: A politician is endlessly insulted and finds himself isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' takes the T from INSULT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular describes something isolated, like an island, detached from outside influences.

clue.text: Devil sure to catch sinner finally, it's clear

parts.note: a demon is a devil

indicators.note: to catch means to hold something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: stable means steady and secure, sure

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of sinner

explanation.surface: A devil is confident of trapping a wrongdoer in the end, plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' takes R from sinner, which 'to catch' puts inside STABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something demonstrable can be shown or proved, so its truth is evident and plain.

clue.text: Leave country missing head of Gulf state

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: to emigrate is to leave one's country to live elsewhere

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of Gulf

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a nation without its Gulf leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gulf state' reads as one phrase, but Gulf supplies the G removed and state alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a territory ruled by an emir, a kind of state, as in the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Went by ebbing river putting legs in

indicators.note: in places the stages of a race within the turned river
ebbing means flowing back, so the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales and England, a crossword favourite
legs and laps are both stages of a race or journey

explanation.surface: Someone passed a receding river and stepped into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legs' are not limbs but stages of a race, as in the legs of a relay.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has elapsed has passed or gone by.

clue.text: Tell apart iced martinis, shaken or stirred

indicators.note: a cocktail shaken or stirred has its contents mixed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A James Bond style drinker claims to distinguish a shaken martini from a stirred one.
explanation.definitionFit: To discriminate is to perceive the difference between things, to distinguish them.

clue.text: Exposed rock cut with poor rocks

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes or unsettles, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A geology note about bare stone cut through with inferior rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' looks like more geology but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is part of the bedrock visible at the surface, rock left bare.

clue.text: They're useless without point at the end

definitions.text: They're useless without point at the end

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: needless means unnecessary, of no use
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A remark that sewing pins are worthless if they lose their sharp tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end' says which S of NEEDLESS goes. Read whole, the clue also defines: sewing needles are no use blunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing tools lacking a sharp tip cannot pierce cloth, so the whole clue describes them.

clue.text: Hand includes length for inch

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a side or hand is a team of players, as in a card game; also either side as in on the other hand

explanation.surface: A measuring note: a hand contains enough length to stand for an inch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' and 'inch' look like units of measure; inch is a verb, to edge along.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to move sideways furtively, edging or inching along.

clue.text: Financial officer's safe in top of Trump Tower

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of Trump
in places the word for safe within the word for tower

parts.note: to rear is to rise high, to tower
sure means safe or secure, as in a sure footing

explanation.surface: A money manager's strongroom is at the top of Trump Tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump Tower' reads as the New York building; Trump gives only T, and Tower is a verb meaning to rear up.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the official responsible for an organisation's funds.

clue.text: Record cheers topping popular cheer

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece topping another sits above it

parts.note: to enter data is to record it
ta is British informal for thanks, as is cheers
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A hit record with cheering on top of a popular cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you, matching cheers in its sense of thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain is to amuse or gladden, to cheer people up.

clue.text: Going into raptures is tantalisingly tough

indicators.note: going into means the answer lies inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: Falling into ecstasy is teasingly hard to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resistant withstands force or damage, being hard and durable.

clue.text: Mug reportedly provides comfort

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the spoken form counts and not the spelling

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a sucker

explanation.surface: A drinking mug brings solace, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is not a cup but a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is help and support given in a time of need, a form of comfort.

clue.text: Brains addled comprehending European national

indicators.note: comprehending means including within, so one piece goes inside the other
addled means muddled, so the letters of brains are mixed up

explanation.surface: Muddled minds struggle to understand a citizen of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European national' reads as one phrase, but European gives only E and national alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country; this one belongs to Serbia in the Balkans.

clue.text: Best stuff contains energy

indicators.note: contains means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to stuff and to cram both mean to pack tightly
E is the standard symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: The finest food is packed with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best stuff' reads as a phrase, but stuff is a verb meaning cram.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream is the finest part of something, as in the cream of the crop.

clue.text: Cup of tea cold in lounge

parts.note: cha is informal British for tea

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for cold within the word for lounge

parts.note: to lie about is to lounge
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cup of cooling tea in a sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' is a verb here, to lie, not a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a goblet, especially the cup used for wine at Communion.

clue.text: Famous rapper almost not without love

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Eminem is a famous American rapper

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed from not

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A well-known rapper is nearly unloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the final M from EMINEM; 'without love' drops the O from not, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent describes someone distinguished and well known in their field.

clue.text: Coarse material from two males?

parts.note: rough cloth seemingly sourced from two male beasts; in fact the names of a male deer and a male sheep simply join

explanation.surface: Rough cloth obtained from a pair of male animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the males are not a source of fibre: a buck and a ram simply join to give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiff, coarse cotton or linen cloth used in bookbinding and to stiffen garments.

clue.text: Wild bloke in charge

parts.note: bloke is informal British for a man

explanation.surface: A frenzied fellow is the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes frenzied, uncontrolled excitement, behaviour that is wild.

clue.text: Order again proper drink, one to start

parts.note: real means genuine, proper

indicators.note: one is the Roman numeral I, and to start says that letter moves to the front of the drink

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A customer reorders a proper drink, one to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order again' suggests buying another round; here order means arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to arrange or put into line afresh, to set in order once more.

clue.text: New top mark rejected from public school

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, top, written here as AI
a note is a mark, as in take note

explanation.surface: A new top grade is withheld from a private school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top mark' looks like a single grade, but it is A1 then NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Boy of Eton, England's best-known fee-paying school, is described this way, so it means belonging to that school.

clue.text: Insect eats fruit for nourishment

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an ant is an insect
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A bug feeds on fruit to get its food.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for food or sustenance.

clue.text: Sublime time passed with finish in Cologne?

parts.note: ran, as in time ran on, means passed

indicators.note: in places the word for finish within the word for cologne

parts.note: eau de cologne is a perfume, a scent
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A sublime moment at the end of a visit to the German city of Cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cologne' looks like the German city, but the question mark hints at eau de cologne, a scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Transcendent means surpassing the ordinary, supreme, much as sublime does.
